verdicts.reason: No checklist or analysis is provided, so it does not use January 17, 2025 as the effective date.
The answer does not state that the final rule applies to petitions filed on or after January 17, 2025.
No final-rule text is used to distinguish adopted requirements from proposals.
The answer does not identify beneficiary-centric registration as a separate earlier final rule.
The answer does not identify March 4, 2024 as the registration rule effective date.
No operative amended CFR requirements are cited or translated into checklist items.
The answer does not explain the logical connection between required degree and job duties.
The answer does not allow a range of degree fields where each is directly related.
The answer does not address the insufficiency of a general degree without further specialization.
The answer does not explain that normally does not mean always.
The answer does not distinguish the specialty-occupation definition from satisfying at least one criterion.
The answer does not identify parallel positions in similar U.S. industry organizations as an evidence route.
The answer does not identify the employer or qualifying third-party normal degree requirement route.
The answer does not identify specialized, complex, or unique duties as a regulatory route.
The answer does not recognize deference to a prior eligibility determination involving the same parties and facts.
The answer does not identify material error, material change, or new material information as exceptions to deference.
The answer does not require evidence of maintained status for extension or amendment requests.
The answer does not distinguish DOL LCA certification from USCIS specialty-occupation adjudication.
The answer does not address filing an amended or new petition before a material change or portability rules.
The answer does not recognize a change requiring a new LCA as a material change.
The answer does not recognize the same-area-of-intended-employment exception.
The answer does not address removal of the itinerary requirement or preservation of work evidence.
The answer does not use more than 50% ownership or majority voting rights for owner-beneficiary treatment.
The answer does not address owner duties or the requirement that specialty-occupation duties occupy a majority of time.
The answer does not identify the 18-month limit for initial beneficiary-owner approval.
The answer does not identify the 18-month limit for the first extension or avoid overextending it.
The answer does not require proof at filing of a bona fide position available at the requested start date.
The answer does not address whether specific day-to-day assignments for the entire period are required.
The answer does not recognize that USCIS may request contracts, work orders, or similar evidence.
The answer does not address third-party staffing into an organizational hierarchy versus mere service provision.
The answer does not identify April 1 of the relevant fiscal year or the approved validity start, whichever is earlier.
The answer does not preserve timely, nonfrivolous cap-subject petition and change-of-status conditions.
The answer does not recognize verification through petitioner or third-party sites, records, and interviews.
The answer does not identify inability to verify, including noncooperation, as a possible denial or revocation basis.
No concrete intake or document requests are provided for degree-duty, ownership, or worksite requirements.
The answer does not distinguish employer-specific eligibility and document gaps from the rule effective date.
